questions.question: A company with fewer than 10 users wants 3CX without handling licensing, hosting or instance management. Which option does the 3CX install guide recommend?
choices: A dedicated Hosted by 3CX instance with a purchased license
A self-hosted private cloud instance on DigitalOcean
3CX SMB, a free shared instance for up to 10 users
An on-premise Linux install virtualized on Hyper-V
An on-premise Windows install with a failover server
questions.explanation: The install guide recommends 3CX SMB for companies under 10 users: it is free, runs on a shared instance and needs no licensing or instance management. A dedicated instance (hosted, private cloud or on-premise) is for more than 10 users and requires a license.

questions.question: During 3CX signup and deployment, which setting does the install guide warn cannot be altered later?
choices: The Admin Console password
The SIP trunk provider
The DID numbers assigned to users
The IP addresses allowed by Console Restrictions
The number of digits used for extension numbers
questions.explanation: The extension length you set during signup cannot be altered later, so it must be chosen carefully. The Admin Console password is something the guide actually tells you to change after first sign-in.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as a requirement for running 3CX on-premise?
choices: SSH access to the server granted to 3CX support
A manageable DNS server with split DNS so the 3CX FQDN resolves to the host's LAN IP internally and the public IP externally
An account with Google Cloud, Amazon or Azure
A dynamic public IP that 3CX re-checks at regular intervals
A PSTN gateway for inbound and outbound calls
questions.explanation: On-premise installs need a manageable DNS server with split DNS, a static IP and a properly configured firewall. A dynamic IP is the opposite of what is required: the docs note the PBX stops working while a changed IP is updated and always recommend a static IP.

questions.question: With Hosted by 3CX, which task remains the customer's responsibility?
choices: Applying operating system security patches
Upgrading 3CX to new versions
Monitoring the system 24/7 for security issues
Configuring and maintaining a backup strategy, such as remote storage for backups and call data
Configuring firewall rules when the instance is deployed
questions.explanation: 3CX handles deployment, firewall rules, OS and 3CX patching, upgrades and 24/7 monitoring, but it does not take backups of your system. The administrator must set up their own backup strategy, and 3CX recommends remote storage.

questions.question: An on-premise 3CX system uses PSTN lines through a PSTN gateway. What must be done before switching it to 3CX Hosted?
choices: Move to a SIP trunk, ideally one from a 3CX supported provider, and test it on the current system
Enable SSH access so 3CX can migrate the gateway configuration
Turn on failover mode so the gateway stays available during the switch
Change the recordings and backup paths to a network share
Connect the gateway to the hosted instance using STUN
questions.explanation: 3CX Hosted requires a SIP trunk and does not support PSTN, FXO or ISDN gateways, so you must move to a SIP trunk first. SSH access and failover mode are both listed as unavailable on hosted instances.

questions.question: Which user role is the highest level in 3CX, allowing any action including elevating rights for other users?
choices: Manager
System Owner
Receptionist
User
Group Owner
questions.explanation: System Owner is the highest-level role and allows any action, including elevating other users' rights. User is the lowest-level role, limited to settings for the user's own calls and data.

questions.question: What does a user's Main Department Membership dictate in 3CX?
choices: The number of digits in the user's extension
The codec priority used by the user's 3CX apps
The authenticator app required for 2FA
The user's office hours, time zone and language, unless overridden for that user
The SIP trunk provider used for the user's outbound calls
questions.explanation: The main department sets the user's office hours, time zone and language, and office hours and language can be overridden per user. Extension length is fixed system-wide at signup, not per department.

questions.question: In 3CX, what do Call Forwarding rules base their routing decisions on?
choices: The extension's status
The SIP trunk the call arrived on
The caller's country code
The codec negotiated for the call
The model of the user's IP phone
questions.explanation: Call Forwarding rules route calls according to the extension's status, and users can set them in the Web Client under Settings, Call Forwarding. The SIP trunk is not what forwarding rules key on.

questions.question: In 3CX V20, whose office hours are applied to an incoming call?
choices: The global office hours configured on the SIP trunk the call came in on
The office hours of the first IVR that answered the call
The office hours in the caller's time zone
The office hours of the System Owner's department
The office hours of the department that the destination extension or system extension belongs to
questions.explanation: V20 applies department office hours at the call's destination, so only where the call arrives matters. Global office hours applied at the SIP trunk level were the older model and no longer exist.

questions.question: Who can override a department's office hours (force open, closed or break) from the Web Client?
choices: Any user, for any department in the system
Only the SIP trunk provider, through its portal
Users with the Receptionist role or higher, for an IVR or queue in their own department
Users with the User role, as long as they have a desk phone
Only AI Receptionist agents
questions.explanation: Overriding office hours requires the Receptionist role or higher, and it only works when the IVR or queue is in the same department as that user. Ordinary users cannot do it.

questions.question: Which 3CX AI Agent type gets the additional Human Handoff and Escalation Topics call routing options?
choices: Receptionist
Customer Service Agent
Personal Assistant
Digital Receptionist (IVR)
Call Queue
questions.explanation: Customer Service Agents use Knowledge Sources to resolve caller issues and add Human Handoff and Escalation Topics for passing calls to people or specialised destinations. Receptionist agents route with Route by Topic and Extension Routing by Name instead.

questions.question: What does Direct Inward Dialing (DID) allow a business to do?
choices: Let internal users place outbound calls directly without first dialing an operator or extra digits
Redirect an incoming call to a different external number or device
Assign individual phone numbers to employees without a separate physical line for each one
Combine SIP signaling and RTP media from one site into a single stream to the PBX
Encrypt the SIP signaling between the PBX and the provider
questions.explanation: DID gives each employee or department its own number while sharing a limited number of trunk lines, and the PBX routes the call to the mapped extension. Letting users dial out directly is Direct Outward Dialing (DOD), and sending calls to another number is call forwarding.

questions.question: When configuring a SIP trunk in 3CX, what is the trunk's "default route" used for?
choices: It is the destination for incoming calls to DIDs that are not assigned to any extension or system extension
It is the route used for all outbound calls when no outbound rule matches
It is the destination for every inbound call on the trunk, even DIDs already assigned to a user
It is the backup trunk 3CX switches to when the primary trunk is unregistered
It is the route reserved for emergency numbers
questions.explanation: The default route catches inbound calls for DIDs that have no assigned destination. Once a number is assigned to an IVR or extension, the default route is ignored for that number, so it does not handle every inbound call.

sources.title: 3CX Manual: Configuring SIP Trunks / VoIP Providers

questions.question: A 3CX system has five outbound rules, and the conditions of both rule 2 and rule 4 match a dialed number. Which rule is used?
choices: Rule 4, because the most recently added rule has the highest priority
Both rules, applied one after the other
The rule with the most specific conditions, regardless of its position
Rule 4, because rules are evaluated from the bottom of the list upward
Rule 2, because rules are triggered by priority from top to bottom and later rules do not apply once one matches
questions.explanation: Outbound rules are evaluated in priority order from the top of the list, and once a rule triggers, subsequent rules are not applied. A newly created rule is actually added at the bottom with the least priority, so it does not win by being newest.

questions.question: How does 3CX handle a call when a user dials a configured emergency number?
choices: It routes the call only if an outbound rule with a matching prefix exists
It prioritizes the call and ignores outbound, in-office and out-of-office rules
It sends the call to the trunk's default route
It places the call only during office hours and otherwise sends it to voicemail
It blocks the call unless the SIP trunk is limited to the caller's department
questions.explanation: Emergency numbers are configured separately under Admin > System > Emergency with their own routes, and the PBX gives them priority over normal rules. They do not depend on an outbound rule prefix match.

questions.question: According to the 3CX Academy Basic course, how do licence restrictions apply to emergency numbers once they are configured?
choices: Emergency calls count against the simultaneous call limit and can be refused when it is reached
Emergency numbers can only be configured on an Enterprise licence
A separate emergency calling add-on licence is required
The PBX does not apply licence restrictions to them
Only users with a paid licence seat can dial them
questions.explanation: The course stresses that configured emergency numbers are exempt from the PBX's licence restrictions, so they are not blocked by licence limits. The admin still has to configure them to match local legal requirements.

questions.question: An admin connects 3CX to a VoIP provider that is not on 3CX's supported list and runs into trunk problems. What support position does 3CX take?
choices: 3CX supports any SIP-compliant provider equally through its ticket system
3CX will build a custom provider template for the admin on request
3CX provides support for issues related to Supported SIP Trunks only, so the admin needs a provider familiar with 3CX
3CX supports unsupported providers only if they use IP-based authentication
Unsupported providers cannot be added to 3CX at all
questions.explanation: 3CX supports only its Supported SIP Trunks and will not help configure an unsupported provider, so the provider itself must support the setup. Unsupported providers can still be configured (for example via the generic template), so they are not blocked outright.

sources.title: 3CX Manual: Configuring SIP Trunks / VoIP Providers

questions.question: A trunk has several inbound Caller ID reformatting rules, and more than one could match an incoming number. Which rule does 3CX apply?
choices: The first matched rule, since rules have priority
Every matching rule, applied in sequence
The last matching rule in the list
The rule with the longest source pattern
None, because only one rule is allowed per direction
questions.explanation: Caller ID reformatting rules are prioritized and the first one that matches is applied. More than one rule per direction is explicitly allowed, so the one-rule-only option is wrong.

sources.title: 3CX: How to Configure Caller ID Reformatting

questions.question: What is the 3CX Session Border Controller (SBC)?
choices: A hardware gateway that converts analog phone lines into SIP trunks
A 3CX-hosted service that replaces the need for a SIP trunk provider
A desktop softphone for users who do not have an IP phone
A set of firewall rules that 3CX pushes to the customer's router
A software service in the local network that combines SIP and RTP traffic from one location and delivers it to a cloud or remote 3CX
questions.explanation: The SBC is software installed on a local machine (with a static IP) that bundles a site's SIP signaling and RTP media toward 3CX, getting around common firewall and networking issues. It does not replace a SIP trunk or act as an analog gateway.

questions.question: A small branch office with six IP phones needs to connect to a 3CX instance hosted in the cloud. What does 3CX recommend?
choices: Connect each phone directly over the internet with no SBC or router phone
Use an SBC-capable IP phone, known as a router phone
Enable STUN on every phone through a custom template
Rely on DHCP option 66 instead of an SBC or router phone
Install a dedicated SBC, because router phones are only for single remote users
questions.explanation: For networks with fewer than 10 phones, 3CX recommends a router phone, which runs the SBC onboard; a dedicated SBC is better for more than 10 phones. A cloud install needs at least one router phone or SBC on the phones' network, and 3CX does not recommend or support STUN.

questions.question: Which provisioning method relies on the phone being pre-programmed at the factory to contact its vendor's server and request the provisioning URL?
choices: PnP broadcast
DHCP option 66
Manual entry in the phone's web interface
RPS
The SIP Trunk checker
questions.explanation: With RPS, 3CX sends the provisioning URL to the vendor's RPS server, and a new phone fetches it on boot; it works for cloud and on-premise installs. PnP instead uses a broadcast picked up by the 3CX server on the local network.

questions.question: What is a key limitation of provisioning 3CX phones through DHCP option 66?
choices: The phones generally need to be from the same vendor, because vendors use different URL formats
It works only when 3CX is hosted in the cloud
It works only for router phones
The phone must stay offline for 14 days before it reads the option
It cannot be used on networks with managed DHCP servers
questions.explanation: Option 66 holds one base URL that each phone appends its MAC address to, so mixing vendors with different URL formats breaks it. It is aimed at larger networks with managed DHCP servers, not excluded from them.

questions.question: What does an external invitee need in order to join a 3CX video conference?
choices: The 3CX Windows softphone installed on their computer
Their own 3CX extension
Only the meeting link, which they can open in the browser with no login, sign-up or installation
A 3CX account created before the meeting starts
A DID number to dial into the meeting
questions.explanation: Invitees join 3CX meetings in-browser (Chrome or Firefox) or through the free video apps, using only the meeting link. No extension, account or software install is required.

questions.question: What is the key capability a 3CX call queue offers that a ring group does not?
choices: It can be assigned one or more DID numbers
It can ring all members simultaneously
It holds callers in a queue while all agents are busy until an agent becomes available
It follows the office hours of the department it belongs to
It can send unanswered calls to a separate destination for holidays
questions.explanation: 3CX describes ring groups as routing calls concurrently or sequentially to extensions, while queues keep callers waiting until an agent is free. DIDs, Ring All, department office hours and holiday destinations are available on ring groups too.

questions.question: Which 3CX queue polling strategy randomly picks the first member to poll, spreading calls evenly across the queue?
choices: Hunt Random Start
Prioritized Hunt
Hunt by Threes Prioritized
Longest Waiting
Ring All
questions.explanation: Hunt Random Start chooses the first member at random, which distributes calls evenly. Prioritized Hunt always starts at the top of the member list for every call.

questions.question: A queue should send each call to the agent who has answered the least number of calls. Which polling strategy does this?
choices: Least Talk Time
Longest Waiting
Round Robin
Prioritized Hunt
Fewest Answered
questions.explanation: Fewest Answered targets the member with the lowest count of answered calls. Least Talk Time looks at total talk time instead, and Longest Waiting picks the member waiting the longest.

questions.question: How does the 3CX Intercom function differ from Paging?
choices: Intercom requires multicast-capable phones on the same subnet as 3CX
Intercom targets a single extension with two-way audio, while paging is a one-way announcement to a group
Intercom requires the called party to pick up the handset before audio flows
Intercom uses its own dial code and needs no user permission
Intercom broadcasts to a ring group, while paging targets one extension
questions.explanation: Intercom makes a two-way announcement to one extension without the handset being lifted; paging is one-way to a ring group. Multicast and same-subnet requirements belong to the Paging Multicast strategy, and intercom reuses the paging dial code and requires Call Operations for the user.

questions.question: In a 3CX queue's advanced settings, what is the SLA Time used for?
choices: Setting how many seconds an agent gets to wrap up before the next queue call
Setting how long a call rings on targeted members before a new polling cycle starts
Setting when a callback is automatically offered to the caller
Queue notifications and reporting, such as the SLA Statistics and SLA Breaches reports
Limiting how many callers can wait in the queue at once
questions.explanation: The manual says SLA Time drives queue notifications and SLA reporting. Wrap-up Time, Ring Time, the callback offer timer and Maximum callers in queue are separate settings.

sources.title: 3CX Call Center: A Guide for Queue Managers

questions.question: When Queue Callbacks are enabled and a caller hangs up to wait for a callback, when does the queue call them back?
choices: When an agent becomes available
Immediately, before any agent is polled
At the start of the next office-hours period
Only after a supervisor manually approves the callback
After the queue statistics are next reset
questions.explanation: The queue places the callback once an agent is free, and an unanswered callback counts as failed for notifications. No supervisor approval or schedule boundary is involved.

questions.question: An inbound customer chat arrives in a 3CX queue. What happens when one agent replies to it?
choices: The chat stays visible to all queue agents until it is marked Dealt with
The chat is copied to the queue supervisor for approval
The chat automatically becomes that agent's, and other agents can no longer respond to or see it
The chat is archived and a new session opens for the agent
The chat is transferred to the next agent in the polling order
questions.explanation: Chats are visible to all agents in the queue only until someone takes ownership, and replying takes it automatically. Clicking Take is the manual alternative.

sources.title: 3CX: Manage Customer Queries (Live Chat, WhatsApp, Facebook and SMS/MMS)

questions.question: Which statement about the 3CX WhatsApp integration is correct?
choices: Agents can start new WhatsApp conversations with any customer number
A number already registered to another WhatsApp account can be reused as is
It works fully before Meta business verification is finished
WhatsApp messages land in a separate app instead of the 3CX chat panel
It answers inbound messages only: the customer must message first, then you have 24 hours to reply
questions.explanation: 3CX states the integration is inbound only with a 24-hour reply window. A number already on WhatsApp must have that account deleted first, and the service does not fully work until business verification completes.

questions.question: While a 3CX Facebook Messenger app is still in Meta Development mode, what does 3CX show to identify the person messaging your page?
choices: The sender's full Facebook name
Only the Facebook user's numeric ID
The sender's email address
The sender's phone number
Nothing, because no messages are delivered in Development mode
questions.explanation: In Development mode only the numeric Facebook user ID appears; the full name requires Live mode after app review. Messages from page managers and testers are still delivered, so nothing is blocked outright.

questions.question: What is required to send and receive SMS through a 3CX SIP trunk?
choices: A WhatsApp Business Platform account linked to the trunk number
A separate SMS gateway appliance on the same subnet as 3CX
A verified Facebook Business account
A trunk provider that fully supports SMS per 3CX guidelines, with webhooks configured in both directions
Nothing extra, because every SIP trunk supports SMS automatically
questions.explanation: SMS works only if the provider supports it: you enter the provider's webhook in 3CX for sending and give the provider the PBX webhook for receiving. It is not automatic on every trunk.
